{"retrieved_sources": {"BRD-K08109215": [{"source_id": "pubchem:46943432:description:1", "text": "Molibresib is a member of the class of triazolobenzodiazepine that is 4H-[1,2,4]triazolo[4,3-a][1,4]benzodiazepine substituted by methyl, 2-(ethylamino)-2-oxoethyl, 4-chlorophenyl, and methoxy groups at positions 1, 4S, 6, and 8, respectively. It is an orally bioavailable inhibitor of BET family of proteins that has demonstrated antitumour activity in preclinical models of solid and hematologic malignancies. It has a role as a bromodomain-containing protein 4 inhibitor, an antineoplastic agent and an apoptosis inducer. It is a secondary carboxamide, a triazolobenzodiazepine, an aromatic ether and a member of monochlorobenzenes.", "provider": null, "url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/searchId.do?chebiId=CHEBI:95082"}], "BRD-K11528507": [], "BRD-K49328571": [{"source_id": "pubchem:3062316:description:1", "text": "Dasatinib (anhydrous) is an aminopyrimidine that is 2-methylpyrimidine which is substituted at position 4 by the primary amino group of 2-amino-1,3-thiazole-5-carboxylic acid and at position 6 by a 4-(2-hydroxyethyl)piperazin-1-yl group, and in which the carboxylic acid group has been formally condensed with 2-chloro-6-methylaniline to afford the corresponding amide. A multi-targeted kinase inhibitor, it is used, particularly as the monohydrate, for the treatment of chronic, accelerated, or myeloid or lymphoid blast phase chronic myeloid leukemia. Note that the name 'dasatinib' is used to refer to the monohydrate (USAN) as well as to anhydrous dasatinib (INN). It has a role as an anticoronaviral agent, an antineoplastic agent and a tyrosine kinase inhibitor. It is a monocarboxylic acid amide, an organochlorine compound, an aminopyrimidine, a member of 1,3-thiazoles, a N-arylpiperazine, a N-(2-hydroxyethyl)piperazine, a secondary amino compound and a tertiary amino compound. It is a conjugate base of a dasatinib(1+).", "provider": null, "url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/searchId.do?chebiId=CHEBI:49375"}], "BRD-K56343971": [{"source_id": "pubchem:42611257:description:1", "text": "Vemurafenib is a pyrrolopyridine that is 1H-pyrrolo[2,3-b]pyridine which is substituted at position 5 by a p-chlorophenyl group and at positions 3 by a 3-amino-2,6-difluorobenzoyl group, the amino group of which has undergone formal condensation with propane-1-sulfonic acid to give the corresponding sulfonamide. An inhibitor of BRAF and other kinases. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent and a B-Raf inhibitor. donors.reason: BET bromodomain inhibitor, same class as JQ1-S; most plausible chromatin-reader donor for histone-mark perturbation.
Benzamide/N-acylpiperidine scaffold; only retrieved non-kinase chromatin-adjacent candidate, weak support.

revised_hypotheses: BRD-K08109215 (molibresib/I-BET762) is a BET bromodomain inhibitor like JQ1-S and is the strongest supported donor for transferring a histone-mark response.
BRD-K83189926 has only structural description, not confirmed chromatin pharmacology; support is weak and should be treated cautiously.
Dasatinib and vemurafenib are kinase inhibitors with no retrieved epigenetic mechanism, so they are unsupported as histone-perturbation donors.
Geldanamycin had no retrieved source and cannot be supported.
unresolved: No retrieved source provides measured A375 histone responses for any donor; target-minus-A375 transfer values remain unavailable.
Whether any donor yields a reproducible >0.5 log2 histone perturbation versus vehicle cannot be established from the supplied pharmacology descriptions alone.
BRD-K11528507 (geldanamycin) had no retrieved source and was excluded.
